main.content:
==English==
{{number box|en|60}}

===Etymology===
{{inh+|en|enm|sixty}}, {{m|enm|sexty}}, {{inh|en|ang|sixtiġ}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*sehs tigiwiz|t=sixty}}, equivalent to {{af|en|six|-ty<id:multiple>}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|sexty}}, {{m|sco|saxty|t=sixty}}, {{cog|stq|säkstich|t=sixty}}, {{cog|fy|sechstich|t=sixty}}, {{cog|nl|zestig|t=sixty}}, {{cog|nds-de|sesstig|t=sixty}}, {{cog|de|sechzig|t=sixty}}, {{cog|sv|sextio|t=sixty}}, {{cog|no|seksti|t=sixty}}, {{cog|is|sextíu|t=sixty}}. Compare also {{cog|sa|षष्टि}}.

* {{hyph|en|six|ty}}

===Numeral===
{{head|en|numeral}}

# {{sid|en|Q79998}} The cardinal number occurring after fifty-nine and before sixty-one, represented in Roman numerals as [[LX]] and in Arabic numerals as 60.
#: {{syn|en|threescore|qq=archaic}}
#* {{RQ:New Yorker|author=Henry Alford|title=Not a Word|date=2005-08-21|url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2005/08/29/not-a-word|passage={{...|The investigator first removed from contention any word that was easily recognized or that appears in Webster’s Third New International;}}the remaining three hundred and '''sixty''' words were then vetted with a battery of references. Six potential Mountweazels emerged.
|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170309051436/https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2005/08/29/not-a-word}}
